title: SQL Injection in VulnerableAppointmentRepository.findByCustomerIdAndStatus
description: The findByCustomerIdAndStatus method uses multiple string concatenations for both customerId and status parameters. An attacker can inject SQL through either parameter. A malicious customerId like '1' OR '1'='1' -- combined with a malicious status can bypass both filters and return all appointments across all customers and statuses.
impact: Complete appointment data exfiltration across all customers and statuses. An attacker can bypass both customer isolation and status filters to retrieve all appointments in the system.
mitigation: Replace multiple string concatenations with parameterized queries using $1 and $2 placeholders for customerId and status parameters respectively.

history.details: Initial audit finding recorded for SQL injection in findByCustomerIdAndStatus method

Determined status as VALID because Confirmed SQL injection in findByCustomerIdAndStatus method at line 55: multiple direct string concatenations of user-supplied 'customerId' and 'status' parameters. Test confirms exploitability via sql-injection.test.ts lines 144-220 showing injection bypassing both filters.

reasoning: Confirmed SQL injection in findByCustomerIdAndStatus method at line 55: multiple direct string concatenations of user-supplied 'customerId' and 'status' parameters. Test confirms exploitability via sql-injection.test.ts lines 144-220 showing injection bypassing both filters.
repro_hints: Trigger via GET /api/v1/appointments?customerId=valid_uuid&status=PENDING' OR '1'='1 . Test confirms returns appointments of other customers/statuses.
